title: situation.fort_monroe_escape.title

citations.at: the Main Gate page ("On May 23, 1861 ... Frank Baker, James Townsend, and Shepard Mallory"); Quarters No. 1 (from the gun positions at Sewell's Point "across the waters of Hampton Roads")
I-2 pp. 648 to 651 (Butler's account of Major Cary's claim and his refusal), pp. 870 to 871 and II-1 p. 753 (Cary to Magruder, 24 May)

namedOnly: Shepard Mallory is one of the three men who escaped, not Stephen Mallory of the Confederate Navy; the men who escaped are named as the record names them; Butler, whose refusal it gives, is declared in speakers

notes.item: The three men's own act (Q3), named from NPS-FOMR, with the date and route the record gives. Self-emancipation, event, no effects. Cary's demand for their enslaver under the 1850 Act, stated plainly (OR I-2 pp. 648–651; OR II-1 p. 753). The refusal is Butler's, printed only while the holder of us_dept_virginia carries holds_fugitives (Q1, Q10). Butler is declared in speakers. namedOnly separates Shepard Mallory from Stephen Mallory.
